finalText:
I didn't change anything in response to the check's errors. They're wrong, and following them would have damaged the board.

The check said all 300 elements on the GitPanel board are new and need `"author": {"kind": "ai"}`. But apart from the Unsorted section I created, every one of those elements was already on the board in the last commit. Each one is credited to a person (Tereza, Jonas, Ivana, Marek or Petra), and the file still credits them exactly the same way.

Doing what it asked would have:
- credited 300 people's stickies, sections, notes, shapes and arrows to the AI;
- changed three locked stickies: Marek's "keep the student tier" in Pricing and two in Done.

When I ran `maude design check .design/ui-gitpanel.annotations.json` directly, it reported "✓ 1 file(s) ok". So the end-of-run check seems to be comparing against the wrong starting point and treating the whole board as new. The fault is likely in that end-of-run check, not in the board.

The board is as I left it: all 60 loose stickies are in the Unsorted section, which is credited to AI, and every other element still has its original author.
